chunks.title: THE CLAIMANT
chunks.transcript:
That was the first time my name sounded different in his mouth.

Not important.

Not friendly.

Placed.

Like he had put it somewhere and intended to find it again.

I rubbed my thumb across the edge of my rank pin.

The Authority mark caught against the nail.

Low B-class.

Named Ranker.

Peg-Leg Greg, according to people who had never asked whether I wanted the fucking thing attached to me.

Ithar watched the hand.

Of course he did.

The right hand that no longer closed all the way.

The shoulder that sat slightly wrong under my coat.

He took his time looking.

Then he spoke again.

chunks.title: THE CLAIMANT
chunks.transcript:
His eye flicked to the pin on my coat.

“Not like this.”

The current badge had my class stamped beneath the Authority seal.

B.

The letter was honest.

I had worked hard for it.

It still felt strange every time I looked down.

“S-class.”

Ithar waited.

I had not expected applause.

Still.

The dragon let the silence stretch until I understood he was not going to help me define my own word.

chunks.title: THE CLAIMANT
chunks.transcript: “Not black. Purple. The membrane was a pressure bladder. You did not know that. Good. A fabricated memory may contain detail. A repeated story may acquire texture. A person may be told an event so often that they remember the telling as experience. None of those possibilities are especially interesting by themselves.

chunks.title: THE CLAIMANT
chunks.transcript:
“Nhal was one of several things she called herself. I knew that name. In the history I know, she has not spoken to a human in one hundred and twelve years. If she gave you my name, tell me when you met her, where, and what condition made the meeting possible. I am not asking for the entire story yet. I am asking for enough to identify the path you claim existed.”

Late.

Forty-eight, maybe forty-nine.

Under the salt flats north of Vey.

She did not live there.

She was trapped there.

chunks.title: THE CLAIMANT
chunks.transcript:
Ithar's eye half closed.

I had started to recognize that too.

Not refusal exactly.

Priority.

“You haven't even looked at it.”

He had looked at me.

That was not better.

“What do you want?”

The eye opened fully.

Ithar shifted more comfortably into the gold.

“The Line is why you came today. It is not why you knew my name before the western stations began failing, or why you knew the mountain before you climbed it, or why your body reaches for movements this body has not learned.

chunks.title: THE BARGAINER
chunks.transcript:
That was the problem with talking to something that could probably sit in the same position longer than I had been alive.

There was no body language to wait out.

No awkwardness to exploit.

No point where the other person glanced at the door because they had somewhere else to be.

I had somewhere else to be.

Several million people did too.

The dragon had a cave.

I was starting to suspect that was the stronger negotiating position.

Ithar's attention shifted.

Not away from the problem.

chunks.transcript:
I decided not to ruin it by mentioning it.

“What do you want?”

The answer came as a territory, not a word.

“You. More precisely, your account.

“The discrepancy began with you. Your Line knowledge may be consequence, coincidence, or merely one expression of the same event. The name is another. Nhal is another. Your body attempting movements it has not learned is another. Your present rank is not the interesting part. The habits your body displays despite that rank are.

chunks.title: THE BARGAINER
chunks.transcript:
“You are sixty soon. Your species measures a life in decades and then behaves surprised when there are not enough of them. You are not surprised. That interests me.

“You have been searching for me for years. You have already lived two lives by your own description. You arrived with enough food to reach me, not enough to return comfortably. Your planning prioritizes arrival over departure.

“I do not know what conclusion belongs to those facts yet. I know only that they belong in the account.”

chunks.transcript:
I regretted several answers I had not even said out loud.

“I can hunt.”

His eye dropped to the leg.

“Poorly.”

That one I admitted for him.

The word perhaps sat between us without being spoken.

I had come here to save the Line.

Perhaps.

I looked at the passage again.

The exit did not help.

“What if I say no?”

The dragon answered without ceremony.

“You leave. You may die on the mountain. You may live. The Line may fail. I will not burn you for refusing conversation.”
